newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA CEN BANK INTERVENES TO KEEP LEU LOW.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA CEN BANK INTERVENES TO KEEP LEU LOW.

text.p: Operators on Romania's foreign exchange market said on Wednesday that the central bank had intervened to prevent the leu from appreciating after standing at 7,050/90 to the dollar for days.
"We are certain that the National Bank bank has intervened and bought large amounts of dollars," one dealer with a private bank said.
The leu closed the day weaker at 7,120/180 to the dollar.
"It is clear that their (BNR) action is meant to prevent the leu from firming." the dealer said.
BNR spokesman Mugur Stet denied any intervention by the bank saying Wednesday's dollar purchases had been in line with the central bank's policy to build up reserves.

"I admit we bought fairly large amounts of dollars over the past weeks," Stet told Reuters. "We had to buy because the market started being flooded with hard currency from portfolio investors to the capital market. So we had to take action," he said.
On Tuesday, Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea said the BNR's foreign exchange reserves stood at $1.6 billion, double the level recorded in February.

However, operators said on Wednesday the BNR had placed buying orders with a firm quotation by mid-day, departing from the "regular" pattern of late trading deals, usually with banks with long positions.
"There is no doubt that the central bank has bought a record amount of dollars from many banks today. It might be a signal to exporters," said another operator.
But dealers declined to elaborate on the range of BNR bids.

The daily Curierul National quoted BNR governor Mugur Isarescu as saying excess dollars on the market, amid a lower demand for credits, could prompt the central bank to intervene to drain the surplus and prevent the leu from firming.
Analysts warned a firmer leu could have a negative impact on reforms, affecting mainly exports and restructuring.
On Wednesday, dealers also said a T-bill issue worth 82 billion lei had not been sufficient to drain leu funds from the money market, in the absence of other banking instruments to mop up the excess.
